name: enmity
quote: That jerk is blocking my career.
description: A deep aversion to the beliefs or actions of another person and a sense they are actively working against your interests.

variations.name: enemy of my enemy
variations.description: A perceived bond with someone who seems to actively dislike your enemy.
examples: unlikely allies working together against a threat

variations.name: enemy signaling
variations.description: Declaring that someone is your enemy mostly to score points with a social group.
examples: Everyone in my family roots against that team, so I do too.

variations.name: habitual enemy
variations.description: Behavior that perpetuates adversarial relations due to past injustice, social cohesion, or identity.

variations.name: former friend
variations.description: Someone who was once a friend that betrayed you.

commentaries.quote: It may be helpful to consider whether to engage your enemy head-on or attempt to understand their perspective. You'll probably end up fighting either way, but the outcome may differ in the long run.
People are bound by countless social threads, so cannot change in the short-term. Don't expect your enemy to change simply because you're punishing them with your anger.
Some people like having an enemy because it gives structure to their lives. Others are fearful of having any enemies lurking.

conditions: A deep aversion to the beliefs or actions of another agent and a sense they are actively working against your interests.
